flagged.title: Context: Caribbean Immigration & British Identity
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states that Scene 5 takes place in Enid's living room (Scenes 2-5 vs 1, 6-8) rather than Mai's bedsit (Scenes 2-4 vs 1, 5-8), which would cause students to fail lesson knowledge checks and make factual errors about the play's dramatic structure.

mark_affecting.quote: This is where scenes two through five take place... Mai's Deptford bedsit, the setting for scenes one, six, seven, and eight.

flagged.title: Scenes 1–3: Enid, Del & the Obeah Woman
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims the news of Mooma's death arrives by letter rather than the iconic telephone call and dropped receiver in Scene 3.

mark_affecting.quote: in Scene 3, another letter arrives. The tension finally snaps and Enid's absolute worst fear from Scene 1 is officially confirmed: Her mother in Jamaica has died.

flagged.title: Scenes 4–7: Generational Conflict
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims that Mai reads Enid's palm in Scene 6 and predicts a long journey, which does not occur in the play and would lose marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: Mai performs one final, crucial act: she reads Enid's palm. Despite all their ideological clashing, Mai gently predicts that Enid is going to make a long journey.

flagged.title: Resolution & the Ending
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Viv participates in the dialogue of Scene 8 ('between Enid, Del, and Viv'), which would cause a student to lose marks for placing Viv in the final scene.

mark_affecting.quote: make the raw, heavy pain between Enid, Del, and Viv feel incredibly genuine

flagged.title: Character Analysis
flagged.reason: The video displays and speaks the misquotation 'No matter how hard I search' instead of 'how much I search' for the play's most critical quotation, teaching students an incorrect quote.

mark_affecting.quote: No matter how hard I search... I'm never there.

flagged.title: Language, Dialect & Identity
flagged.reason: The video heavily reinforces the incorrect claim that Enid speaks standard English with 'linguistic slippage' into patois, which mischaracterises her dialogue throughout the play and would lose students marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: She speaks almost entirely in standard English... She has actively, deliberately cultivated this respectable way of speaking... When Enid's emotional walls come down... bam, her patois just breaks right through that polished standard English surface.

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video devotes an entire section to analyzing a 'printed extract', wrongly preparing students for an extract question when AQA Paper 2 modern text is closed-book with no extract.

mark_affecting.quote: When you see that printed extract, you are going to follow this 1-2-3 punch methodically... Quote it precisely, right from the text in front of you
